captions: Hello, and welcome to Atomic English, Stage 3. In this lesson: Places in town.
Name places in a town and use ‘there is / there are’.
Here are some new words. Library. A place where you borrow books. Hospital.
A place where doctors help sick people. Bakery. A shop that sells bread and cakes.
Listen and say them. library
hospital
bakery.
And some more words. Museum. A building with old and interesting things to see. Station.
A place where trains stop. Bridge. It goes over a river so people can cross.
Listen and say them. museum
station
bridge.
Time for a question. The video will stop.
Which word means: a place where you borrow books?
Now some grammar: there is and there are.
Use ‘there is’ for one thing and ‘there are’ for two or more.
For example: There is a library. For example: There are two parks.
Now listen, and read along. Welcome to Riverton.
Riverton is a small town next to a river.
There is an old stone bridge in the middle of town. There are two bakeries.
The best one is near the station. It sells warm bread every morning.
There is a library with a reading garden, and there is a museum about trains.
There isn't a big shopping centre, but there are lots of small shops.
People in Riverton are friendly.
Another question. The video will stop. Where is Riverton?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like library, hospital, bakery.
You practised there is and there are. And you read Welcome to Riverton.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!

captions: Hello, and welcome to Atomic English, Stage 3. In this lesson: How do I get there?
Ask for and give simple directions.
Here are some new words. Left. The side of the hand you don't usually write with. Right.
The opposite of left. Straight on. Forward, not turning. Listen and say them. left
right
straight on.
And some more words. Corner. Where two streets meet. Opposite.
On the other side, facing. Next to. Very near, at the side of. Listen and say them.
corner
opposite
next to.
Time for a question. The video will stop.
Which word means: the side of the hand you don't usually write with?
Now some grammar: Directions (imperatives).
We give directions with verbs: go, turn, cross, walk.
For example: Turn left at the corner. For example: Go straight on.
Now listen, and read along. Asking the way. Tourist: Excuse me.
How do I get to the museum, please? Kim: Go straight on to the corner. Then turn left.
Tourist: Turn left at the corner. ô kê. Kim: Walk past the bakery.
The museum is on the right, opposite the park. Tourist: Is it far?
Kim: No, it's about five minutes.
Tourist: Thank you very much!
Another question. The video will stop. Where does the tourist want to go?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like left, right, straight on.
You practised directions (imperatives). And you read Asking the way.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!
